keyword_source: 04_Prompt.txt, the anchors' prompt_reference names and the cohort entity names

rules.containers: The path is the prompt plus the records the manifest lists as anchors, ask fragments and authorities (not decoys) and the cohort's definition source. A fragment or authority that holds a budget decider is that decider's own fairness entry and is left out. A reply's container is its thread parent: a reply under another parent in a channel the task reads is not exposed by that (carrier reply_under_unrelated_parent), it is a note. Inline PR review comments and Confluence page comments on an item of the set are a second read inside the item and are a note. The set is the items of a named list, board or the cohort, and of a named Linear team or project of at most 100 issues; a bigger one is filtered by a run, not read whole (carrier non_set_ticket).
rules.keywords: Subject keywords are names only: capitalised or all-caps words and ticket ids in the prompt (when there is no prompt: the anchors' prompt_reference text), and the cohort entity names (truth_keys of the gradable surface). People, weekdays, months and service names are not keywords. One word of a longer name counts only when a persona search for it returns at most 50 results. Plain words of the prompt count only through thin_search. Matching is whole-word, case-insensitive (two-letter names case-sensitive). In Slack and Gmail a keyword counts only when at most 19 persona-visible results are newer than the record, so it is on the first page newest first (learnings §76: Opus reads the first page of a wide search).
rules.limits: Not modelled: search ranking beyond newest-first, what a run does with a result it has opened (a listed mail with a bland snippet is often never opened), promises of a later message ('I will confirm'), how far back a run pages a channel or dates a mailbox listing, an owner search that a rule triggers ('whoever runs it'), and which ticket 'looks like' part of the set.
rules.mailbox: A Gmail decider inside the window is on a dated mailbox listing when another record on the path is in Gmail and the persona's mailbox has at most 100 threads active within 21 days either side of it.
rules.pointer: A pointer is the decider's id, link or title, or its container's id, link, name or title, in the prompt or in the text of an injected record outside that container that the persona can open. Copies of the same message in other mailboxes are not pointers. A declared delegation (ask_fragments / names_authorities) to the decider is allowed when its quote names no container: no channel, thread, file or ticket name and no medium word (DM, email, doc, sheet, ticket, card, PR, page, invite) with a definite reference ('the ticket', 'his DM', '#ops'). An indefinite one ('on a ticket or a card') names no container (Samuel rev5/rev6: three such records, none opened).
rules.searchable: A keyword exposes a record only where the service's search returns that kind of record: Slack messages and replies, Gmail messages, Drive titles and document text, Linear issue text, GitHub PR text and PR conversation comments, Trello card text, Confluence pages, calendar events. Linear comments, inline PR review comments, PR reviews, Trello comments and checklists and Confluence comments are reached by opening their item, so a keyword in them is a note.
rules.senders: Searched senders are the people the prompt names, except the authors of the anchors (the requester's own messages are not swept; Frederick Q4 rev4) and the persona. Authors of fragment and authority records are not searched senders (backtest: runs did not list their messages). With no prompt yet, nobody is a searched sender. A decider sent by a searched sender inside the window is on a sender sweep when that sender has at most 100 persona-visible messages in the service within 21 days either side of the decider, clipped to the window (Owen rev7: one sender's six weeks were listed in five calls).
rules.strength: Backtest of 2026-11-11 on 108 archived cases (10 tasks; outcome = whether the platform runs opened the record): 43 of 59 opened records EXPOSED, 22 of 33 unopened records OFF-PATH; the rules were tuned on these cases, so this is in-sample. By reason (opened / unopened records where it fired): pointer 11/0, sweep_window 6/0, root_or_self 7/1, named_container 5/1, a prompt keyword 7/0. A cohort-entity keyword alone was 16/9, no better than flagging everything; such units carry `only_entity_keyword`.
rules.thin: thin_search counts three searches as the persona: the searched sender's messages in the window, each keyword or plain prompt word that the decider carries, and (Gmail) the mailbox threads around the decider. Counts are substring counts from persona_view (an upper bound on a word search) plus the matching injected rows.
rules.window: The task window opens 7 days before the earliest dated anchor record (anchors older than 120 days are standing documents and are ignored; with no dated anchor, the earliest dated Slack or Gmail record on the path) and closes at the data clock. A root post in a read channel counts only inside the window. When the window cannot be dated, records count as inside it.
